title: Severe bleeding (hemorrhage)
text:
1. Apply firm, direct pressure on the wound with a clean cloth or your hand.
2. Keep pressing continuously — do not lift to check. Add more cloth on top if it soaks through.
3. If possible, raise the injured area above the level of the heart.
4. Lay the person down and keep them warm to prevent shock.
5. Keep pressing until bleeding stops or help arrives. Do not remove any object stuck in the wound — press around it.
source: Philippine Red Cross / WHO First Aid Guidelines

title: Matinding pagdurugo (hemorrhage)
text:
1. Diinan nang mabuti ang sugat gamit ang malinis na tela o ang iyong kamay.
2. Patuloy na diinan — huwag alisin para tingnan. Dagdagan ng tela sa ibabaw kung tumagos ang dugo.
3. Kung kaya, itaas ang nasugatan na bahagi nang mas mataas sa puso.
4. Ihiga ang tao at panatilihing mainit ang katawan para maiwasan ang shock.
5. Patuloy na diinan hanggang tumigil ang dugo o may dumating na tulong. Huwag alisin ang anumang bagay na nakabaon sa sugat — diinan sa paligid nito.
source: Philippine Red Cross / WHO First Aid Guidelines

title: CPR for an adult (not breathing)
text:
1. Check response — tap and shout. If no response and not breathing normally, start CPR.
2. Place the heel of one hand in the center of the chest, other hand on top, fingers interlocked.
3. Push HARD and FAST: at least 5 cm deep, 100–120 pushes per minute. Let the chest rise fully between pushes.
4. If trained, give 30 compressions then 2 rescue breaths. If untrained, do hands-only compressions nonstop.
5. Do not stop until the person breathes, help takes over, or you cannot continue.
source: Philippine Red Cross / American Heart Association CPR Guidelines

title: CPR para sa nasa hustong gulang (hindi humihinga)
text:
1. Tingnan kung may reaksyon — tapikin at sigawan. Kung walang reaksyon at hindi humihinga nang normal, simulan ang CPR.
2. Ilagay ang sakong ng isang kamay sa gitna ng dibdib, ang kabilang kamay sa ibabaw, magkadikit ang mga daliri.
3. Diinan nang MALAKAS at MABILIS: hindi bababa sa 5 cm ang lalim, 100–120 diin kada minuto. Hayaang bumalik nang buo ang dibdib bawat diin.
4. Kung sanay, bigyan ng 30 diin tapos 2 hinga. Kung hindi sanay, tuloy-tuloy na diin lang gamit ang kamay.
5. Huwag huminto hanggang huminga ang tao, may pumalit, o hindi mo na kaya.
source: Philippine Red Cross / American Heart Association CPR Guidelines

title: Choking (adult or child over 1 year)
text:
1. Ask "Are you choking?" If they cannot speak, cough, or breathe, act now.
2. Give 5 back blows: bend them forward, strike firmly between the shoulder blades with the heel of your hand.
3. If still blocked, give 5 abdominal thrusts (Heimlich): stand behind, fist above the navel, grasp with other hand, thrust inward and upward.
4. Alternate 5 back blows and 5 thrusts until the object comes out or they can breathe.
5. If they become unconscious, lower them safely and start CPR.
source: Philippine Red Cross First Aid Guidelines

title: Nabulunan (adulto o batang higit 1 taon)
text:
1. Tanungin "Nabulunan ka ba?" Kung hindi makapagsalita, makaubo, o makahinga, kumilos agad.
2. Bigyan ng 5 palo sa likod: iyuko siya, paluin nang mabuti sa pagitan ng mga balikat gamit ang sakong ng kamay.
3. Kung bara pa rin, bigyan ng 5 diin sa tiyan (Heimlich): tumayo sa likod, kamao sa itaas ng pusod, hawakan ng kabilang kamay, idiin paloob at pataas.
4. Salitan ang 5 palo sa likod at 5 diin hanggang lumabas ang bara o makahinga siya.
5. Kung mawalan ng malay, ibaba nang maingat at simulan ang CPR.
source: Philippine Red Cross First Aid Guidelines

title: Burns (heat, fire, scald)
text:
1. Cool the burn under clean running water for at least 20 minutes. Do NOT use ice.
2. Remove rings, watches, or tight clothing near the burn before it swells — unless stuck to the skin.
3. Do not pop blisters. Do not apply toothpaste, oil, butter, or soy sauce.
4. Cover loosely with a clean, non-stick cloth or cling film.
5. Seek medical help for burns larger than the person's palm, on the face, hands, feet, or genitals, or if the skin is white/charred.
source: WHO / Philippine Red Cross Burn Care Guidelines

title: Paso (init, apoy, banlik)
text:
1. Palamigin ang paso sa ilalim ng malinis na tumatakbong tubig nang hindi bababa sa 20 minuto. HUWAG gumamit ng yelo.
2. Alisin ang singsing, relo, o masikip na damit malapit sa paso bago mamaga — maliban kung nakadikit na sa balat.
3. Huwag putukin ang paltos. Huwag lagyan ng toothpaste, langis, mantikilya, o toyo.
4. Takpan nang maluwag ng malinis na telang hindi dumidikit o cling film.
5. Humingi ng tulong medikal kung mas malaki ang paso kaysa palad, nasa mukha, kamay, paa, o ari, o kung puti/nasunog na ang balat.
source: WHO / Philippine Red Cross Burn Care Guidelines

title: Suspected broken bone (fracture)
text:
1. Keep the injured limb still — do not try to straighten it or push a bone back.
2. Support the limb in the position found using a splint (rolled newspaper, board) and padding.
3. Apply a cold pack wrapped in cloth to reduce swelling.
4. If there is an open wound with the bone, cover with a clean cloth and apply gentle pressure around it to control bleeding.
5. Do not give food or drink in case surgery is needed. Get the person to medical care.
source: Philippine Red Cross First Aid Guidelines

title: Pinaghihinalaang bali ng buto (fracture)
text:
1. Panatilihing hindi gumagalaw ang nasugatang bahagi — huwag subukang ituwid o ibalik ang buto.
2. Suportahan ang bahagi sa posisyong nakita gamit ang splint (nirolyong dyaryo, tabla) at padding.
3. Lagyan ng malamig na compress na nakabalot sa tela para mabawasan ang pamamaga.
4. Kung may bukas na sugat na may lumabas na buto, takpan ng malinis na tela at marahang diinan sa paligid para pigilan ang dugo.
5. Huwag bigyan ng pagkain o inumin dahil baka kailanganin ang operasyon. Dalhin ang tao sa ospital.
source: Philippine Red Cross First Aid Guidelines

title: Snakebite
text:
1. Keep the person calm and still — movement spreads venom faster.
2. Keep the bitten limb BELOW heart level and immobilize it like a fracture.
3. Remove rings, watches, and tight clothing near the bite before swelling.
4. Do NOT cut the wound, suck out venom, apply a tourniquet, or use ice.
5. Note the time of the bite and the snake's appearance if safe. Get to a hospital with antivenom immediately.

title: Kagat ng ahas
text:
1. Panatilihing kalmado at hindi gumagalaw ang tao — ang paggalaw ay mas nagpapabilis ng pagkalat ng kamandag.
2. Panatilihing MAS MABABA sa puso ang nakagat na bahagi at huwag paggalawin tulad ng bali.
3. Alisin ang singsing, relo, at masikip na damit malapit sa kagat bago mamaga.
4. HUWAG hiwain ang sugat, supsupin ang kamandag, lagyan ng tourniquet, o gamitan ng yelo.
5. Tandaan ang oras ng kagat at itsura ng ahas kung ligtas. Dalhin agad sa ospital na may antivenom.

title: Shock (pale, cold, weak, confused)
text:
1. Lay the person down and raise their legs about 30 cm if no leg/spine injury.
2. Keep them warm with a blanket or jacket. Loosen tight clothing.
3. Do NOT give food or drink.
4. Reassure them and keep them still. Turn onto their side if they may vomit or are unconscious but breathing.
5. Monitor breathing. Be ready to start CPR if breathing stops. Get medical help urgently.
source: Philippine Red Cross First Aid Guidelines

title: Shock (maputla, malamig, mahina, nalilito)
text:
1. Ihiga ang tao at itaas ang mga binti ng mga 30 cm kung walang sugat sa binti/gulugod.
2. Panatilihing mainit gamit ang kumot o jacket. Luwagan ang masikip na damit.
3. HUWAG bigyan ng pagkain o inumin.
4. Patahimikin at huwag paggalawin. Ihiga sa tagiliran kung posibleng magsuka o walang malay ngunit humihinga.
5. Bantayan ang paghinga. Maging handa sa CPR kung tumigil ang paghinga. Humingi agad ng tulong medikal.
source: Philippine Red Cross First Aid Guidelines
